exercise: The future of food and agriculture: Alternative pathways to 2050
method: Exploratory quantitative scenarios on alternative driver trends (income, population, productivity, climate)
lessons: Three scenarios is the minimum that avoids a 'good, bad, middle' reading only if each differs on named drivers
notes: Scenario names (business as usual, towards sustainability, stratified societies) from agent knowledge; page read confirms three scenarios and 2050

exercise: The future of food and agriculture: Drivers and triggers for transformation
method: Corporate strategic foresight exercise: 40+ internal experts, about 300-staff survey, external consultation, 18 drivers, quantitative dashboard
number_of_scenarios: 4 (More of the Same; Adjusted Future; Race to the Bottom; Trading Off for Sustainability)
lessons: Pair exploratory scenarios with named 'triggers' (governance, consumer awareness, income distribution, innovation) that move a system between them; fed FAO Strategic Framework 2022 to 2031
notes: Triggers are a template for Vietnam 'robust moves'

exercise: Foresight: The Future of Food and Farming
method: Two-year evidence-led foresight; several hundred experts; challenge framing rather than formal scenarios
lessons: Evidence synthesis builds credibility but, without scenarios or milestones, gives no signposts to track
notes: Primary report not read; journal summary read

exercise: Delivering on EU Food Safety and Nutrition in 2050
method: 9 drivers; 2 axes (global trade; food values); stakeholder workshops; policy stress-test; serious game (Scenario Exploration System)
number_of_scenarios: 4 (Global Food; Regional Food; Partnership Food; Pharma Food)
lessons: Stress-testing found 29 challenges, 8 common to all scenarios: the common ones are the no-regret agenda
notes: Method maps directly onto F10 no-regret moves

exercise: Foresight scenarios for the EU bioeconomy in 2050
notes: Pages returned 403; scenario names not verified

exercise: Quantitative food-system scenario studies (review of 36 studies)
method: Typology: normative types A (one scenario, feasibility) and B (many, conditions); exploratory types C (one variable) and D (many variables)
lessons: State the scenario purpose up front; a vision is a type A or B normative scenario and should not be read as a forecast

exercise: Novel Protein Foods (NPF) backcasting case, Sustainable Technology Development programme
organisation: Dutch inter-ministerial programme; later Profetas research programme
method: Participatory backcasting from a sustainable future vision, followed by a multi-year research programme (Profetas)
lessons: Cited as one of the more successful backcasting cases for follow-up and spin-off; but three decades later Dutch protein policy still lacks measurable targets (VIS-05)
notes: Full texts closed; vision numbers not verified

exercise: Participatory backcasting for European plant-protein production and consumption to 2030
organisation: Universidad Politecnica de Madrid (Manners et al.)
method: Participatory backcasting with interim milestones, barriers, opportunities and actions
lessons: Four strategies (R&D, consumer education, connected supply chains, policy support); actions to reach milestones were needed 'immediately'

exercise: Six backcasting cases in agri-food systems
organisation: Alliance Bioversity-CIAT, Cornell and others (Remans et al.)
method: Four steps: visioning; bottlenecks and solutions; pathway building; reflection and adaptation
lessons: Bundle social and technical innovations; surface trade-offs early; monitoring for adaptive management is the weak link
notes: Includes a Danish national dialogue (2021, 90 people)

organisation: Delft University of Technology (Quist and Vergragt)
method: Five-step participatory framework (problem orientation; vision; backcasting analysis; follow-up agenda; embedding)
lessons: Embedding and follow-up decide impact more than vision quality
notes: Step list from agent knowledge; metadata only read

organisation: Prime Minister's Office (Scenario Planning Office 1995; Strategic Policy Office 2003; Centre for Strategic Futures 2009)
method: Whole-of-government scenario planning and horizon scanning, housed at the centre of government
lessons: Institutional continuity for three decades; foresight sits next to decision makers
notes: Methods detail not on page read

organisation: Prime Minister's Office, Finland; National Foresight Network
method: Report to Parliament each term; ministries' joint foresight group; national network
lessons: A fixed review cycle tied to the political calendar
notes: Start year and Committee for the Future not verified

organisation: NXPO; APEC Center for Technology Foresight (1998); Thailand Foresight Alliance
method: Horizon scanning; 2x2 scenarios; Future Triangle; Mont Fleur and spiderweb scenarios
lessons: Regional foresight hub Vietnam has drawn on since the late 1990s
notes: No food or protein exercise found this wave

exercise: Technology foresight for Vietnam's STI strategy 2021 to 2030
organisation: NISTPASS (Vien Chien luoc va Chinh sach KH&CN)
method: Delphi plus literature on foreign foresight; earlier food-processing foresight pilot (2002)
lessons: Only 15 experts per field; no ranking of priorities; authors advise small, high-quality scenario workshops because statistics are thin

exercise: Vietnam 2035: Toward Prosperity, Creativity, Equity, and Democracy
organisation: World Bank and Ministry of Planning and Investment
method: Aspiration-led joint report with three pillars
lessons: Precedent for a jointly authored national vision; no food or protein content

organisation: IASVN (Southern Agricultural Science and Technology Institute)
method: Three layers: 100-year fixed foundations; 20 to 30-year multiple scenarios; 5 to 10-year implementation and adjustment
lessons: Vietnamese expert voice for 'preparing well for many futures' rather than predicting one

lessons: Annual public verification makes misses visible (feed target cut from 34% to 28%)
